title: Systema Architecture Planner Schema
description: Canonical schema for Systema architecture documents. The document is recursive: every node may contain a subGraph, and nodes inside a subGraph may themselves contain subGraphs without a schema-imposed depth limit. The metadata legend is a superset of the groups: every group must have a corresponding legend entry with the same ID, while the legend may also contain entries for nodes, links, statuses, annotations, or other concepts. A legend entry is not a copy of a group; it contains only legend-specific presentation properties.

legend.description: Superset of the groups. Every data.groups key must have a legend entry with the same key. Additional legend entries are allowed and may describe concepts other than groups.

legendItem.description: Presentation-only legend information. It intentionally does not duplicate the complete Group object. A legend entry may represent a group or another architecture concept.

type.description: Concept represented by this legend entry, e.g. group, node, link, status, annotation, or a domain-specific type.

groups.description: Groups used by nodes in this graph. Every group must have a matching entry in metadata.legend.

group.description: ID of a group defined in the containing graph.

subGraph.description: Recursive graph owned by a node. Every node inside this graph can itself contain another subGraph.

groups.description: Optional graph-local groups. If omitted, nodes may use groups inherited from the parent graph according to the application's group-resolution policy.

source.description: ID of a node in the containing graph.

target.description: ID of a node in the containing graph.

legendIsSupersetOfGroups.description: Every group must be represented in the metadata legend, but the legend may contain additional entries that do not represent groups.
legendIsSupersetOfGroups.rule: set(data.groups.keys()) is a subset of set(metadata.legend.keys())

groupLegendIdentity.description: For every group, the group's object key is its canonical ID and that same ID is used as the legend key.
groupLegendIdentity.rule: for each groupId in data.groups: data.groups[groupId].id == groupId AND metadata.legend[groupId] exists

groupLegendType.description: The legend entry corresponding to a group must identify itself as a group. Other legend entries may use other type values.
groupLegendType.rule: for each groupId in data.groups: metadata.legend[groupId].type == 'group'

legendDoesNotMirrorGroup.description: Legend entries are presentation metadata and do not need to copy all Group properties. Group title, description, and other group properties remain authoritative in data.groups.
legendDoesNotMirrorGroup.rule: legend entries are not required to duplicate Group properties

nodeGroupReference.description: Every node.group must reference a group available to that node's graph.
nodeGroupReference.rule: node.group exists in the containing graph's groups or permitted inherited group scope

recursiveSubGraphs.description: Every node may have a subGraph. A subGraph contains nodes, and those nodes may again have subGraphs recursively without a schema-imposed depth limit.

linkEndpoints.description: Every link source and target must reference nodes in its containing graph.
linkEndpoints.rule: link.source and link.target exist in the containing graph's nodes

uniqueIds.description: Node and link IDs must be unique within their containing graph.
uniqueIds.rule: node.id and link.id are unique within each graph
